M09-negative-control-ledger-order.retirement_reason:
M09 REVERSES THE ORDER OF LEDGER LINES, and this model represents its ledger as
a SEQUENCE: `ledger' = Append(ledger, ...)`, projected by the oracle as a tuple
and compared positionally. Ordering is therefore fully expressible here, the
corpus sees it, and M09 dies under corpus-whole, corpus-slice-led, map-silent
and map-checking on the reference exactly as it did on both arms.

The sealed catalogue's own terms say what to do with this: "a kill here RETRACTS
a documented limit and is a finding". HP-03 retracted the limit. What did not
happen is the consequence -- M09 kept its `control_role` and has been carried as
a red negative control ever since, which means the eval has had NO working
negative control for two rounds.

The retraction is only half true and the other half is the reason a replacement
is needed. Ordering IS invisible to a generated corpus when the modelled thing
is a SET. It is a property of the MODEL, not a limit of corpora, and M09 was
seeded against the one ledger-shaped variable this model happens to represent as
a sequence. A negative control has to be seeded against a variable the model
represents as a set, or it is not testing the limit it claims to test.

M09 is NOT deleted, NOT re-seeded, and NOT excused. It still runs, it is still
scored in the `ordering` class row, and its kills stand as measurements. What it
stops doing is deciding whether the instrument works.

corpus-neg.reason:
M07 is a fault on the ACCEPT path of `reserve`: the hold is one unit too large
on a reservation that succeeds. HP-03's negative corpus contains only DISABLED
edges -- every case asserts a refusal plus inertness -- so it executes no
accepted `Reserve` at all. Zero accepted Reserve cases is not "the negative
corpus missed a blatant fault"; it is the negative corpus doing exactly what it
is for.

Recorded because the shipped arm-B row shows corpus-neg KILLING M07 and a
reader could take that as arm A's instrument being worse. It is not the same
experiment: arm B's M07 is HP-06's declared BROADER-REACH SUBSTITUTE, which
inflates the COMPUTATION of the held total and is therefore observable after any
command including a refusal. Same id, different mutant.

corpus-slice-led.reason:
The LEDGER slice does not project `available` -- M07's only observable -- and
its corpus contains no `Reserve` edge whatsoever (its actions are CloseTenant,
RefuseCloseAlreadyClosed and RefuseCommitUnknown). It cannot execute the
mutated line, and it could not see the difference if it did. That is the
declared shape of an aspect slice, not a miss.
